tools.description: The ResumeMD Markdown conventions for writing a resume: name line, contact line, section headings, role entries, bullets, skills, and the optional sidebar marker — plus a compact skeleton example. tools.name: list_resume_templates
tools.description: All 32 ResumeMD templates with a one-line description of each. The same Markdown renders in every template, so use this to recommend a look for the user (for example: tech for engineers, executive for leadership roles, academic for research CVs). Template ids are also valid input to render_resume_pd

tools.name: analyze_resume
tools.description: Score a Markdown resume 0-100 and get readability metrics, keyword findings (action verbs, technical and soft skills), missing-section checks, and the top improvement recommendations. Runs ResumeMD's free analytics engine on the server — pure computation, no AI call, and the resume is never stored.

tools.name: render_resume_pdf
tools.description: Render a Markdown resume to a finished PDF using a ResumeMD template (default: classic — see list_resume_templates for all 32 ids). findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: analyze_resume · Private data: get_resume_markdown_guide, render_resume_pdf · Public sink: render_resume_pdf.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: analyze_resume · Private data: get_resume_markdown_guide, render_resume_pdf · Public sink: render_resume_pdf

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
